thread:
Marco (CS): customer on 'acme-prod' reporting a spike of 503s/timeouts hitting POST /v1/generate — started ~2026-03-15T09:42Z. They see ~30% error rate and very high tail latency. Customer provided request ids: acme-req-7421, acme-req-7429, acme-req-7450. They're blocked and asking for ETA. Escalating to oncall.
Aisha (Support): thanks. can you paste one full request id + headers and sample payload? model name? sequence length? any images/attachments? @Elisa (Oncall) can you check hosted-prod upstream worker restarts for that timeframe?
Marco (CS): payloads are plain text generation. model: redwood/ggml-13b-v2, max_tokens requested 2048. Notably some prompts are huge — we saw input_length ~18k chars for some calls. Example req id: acme-req-7429. curl sample + headers below:

```

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/ggml-13b-v2","input":"<18k chars>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Body: {"error":"upstream error: worker unavailable","request_id":"acme-req-7429"}

deploy-bot: Deploy started: revision abc123 @ 2026-03-15T09:30:05Z :package:

Elisa (Oncall): I can confirm worker restarts in gpu-pool-17 around 09:40-09:56. Worker node gpu-pool-17/worker-12 shows multiple container restarts (~12 restarts in 15m). Kube events:
```
LastSeen   Type     Reason     Message
09:41:12   Warning  BackOff    Back-off restarting failed container
09:41:12   Normal   Killing    Stopping container for pod inference-worker-12
```
Node metrics just before crash: GPU memory ~96-99%, minor host mem spike. kubectl logs show segfault/cuda assert.

Ben (RuntimeEng): grabbed container logs for acme-req-7429. Relevant tail:
```
[2026-03-15T09:41:10Z] ERROR runtime/kernel.cu: cuda error: device-side assert triggered
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  cuda assert at /build/kernel.cu:421
Stack trace:
  kernel::launch_fused_attention(...)
  runtime::execute_step(...)
signal: Aborted (6) - core dumped
```
Also saw CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED earlier. This pattern looks like a device assert triggered inside our fused attention kernel.

Carmen (MLInfra): correlating with request metadata — many of these failing requests have huge input contexts (seq tokens approaching 21k). Our KV-cache memory grows O(seq_length) and we hit device memory boundary; there's an edge case in our kernel index math that trips a device assert for out-of-bounds when sequence > MAX_KV_WINDOW (which we assumed wouldn't happen). This explains cuda assert -> abort -> container restart.

Aisha (Support): customer is asking for immediate mitigation. Can we reroute them to a fallback model or throttle their requests?

Elisa (Oncall): initiating mitigations now:
- Adding routing override for tenant=acme to model redwood/13b-v2-quant (lower memory footprint)
- Temporarily lowering max_tokens for tenant=acme to 1024 via tenant policy
- Scaling up gpu-pool-17 by +2 nodes to reduce pressure
Applying routing/policy change (control-plane API):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood-internal/api/v1/routing/policies \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"tenant":"acme","route_to":"redwood/13b-v2-quant","max_tokens":1024,"reason":"incident mitigation"}'
```
Update accepted. Scaling requested; nodes provisioning now. Rolling restart of worker-12 in progress.

Marco (CS): CS reports customer confirmed errors dropped to ~1.5% after routing change and scaling. They're able to continue. They want RCA and fix timeline.

Ben (RuntimeEng): collected core dumps and nvcrash logs. Reproducer in local env triggers device assert when seq_length > 20k with current attention kernel. I can reproduce with:
```
# local reproducer (dev env)
python reproduce.py --model ggml-13b-v2 --seq 21000 --dtype fp16
```
Root cause: kernel index calculation overflow for large KV indices in fused attention path. When an out-of-bounds memory index happens on device, NV triggers a device assert which aborts process (SIGABRT). There's no graceful OOM fallback in that path.
I'll push a hotfix to guard index math and add defensive checks returning a controlled error instead of asserting.

Carmen (MLInfra): action items:
- immediate: enforce per-tenant max-context cap 8k and preflight reject too-large requests (HTTP 413)
- short term: deploy hotfix to fused attention kernel to return graceful error and avoid segfaults
- medium term: add quiet-fallback path that spills KV to host for oversized but allowed requests, with clear latency SLO warnings
I've opened tickets: INF-4529 (preflight + tenant caps), INF-4530 (kernel guard), INF-4531 (KV spill design).

Aisha (Support): great. I've notified the customer and scheduled a 1:1 RCA for tomorrow. They want timeline for the hotfix.

Elisa (Oncall): marking incident as mitigated. We'll leave incident open until kernel fix lands. Please post updates in #incidents when the hotfix is deployed. :thumbsup:

Ben (RuntimeEng): hotfix PR created and CI passing; targeting canary deploy tonight and prod rollout tomorrow morning. Will link PR in postmortem.

Marco (CS): customer acknowledged and will wait for formal RCA. Thanks team.

Elisa (Oncall): closing slack thread for now; reopen if regressions appear.
